negative_findings.description: Searches in Montenegrin for investor presentations by ME banks ('prezentacija za investitore', 'investor presentation') surfaced no bank-level investor decks. Montenegrin banks are unlisted or thinly listed and do not produce IR presentation decks the way listed CEE banks do.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ME-bank investor presentation found in this pass; only annual reports, audited statements and bond prospectuses exist as disclosure formats.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief anticipated investor presentations as a KPI source; collection design should instead centre on annual reports + prospectuses + tariffs.

negative_findings.description: No annual-report or reports index page was located in this pass for Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Universal Capital Bank or Zapad banka on their own domains; only CBCG-hosted balance sheets and third-party aggregator profiles were found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Tail banks appear to disclose only via the regulator, not their own sites.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Entity-level card/ATM/POS data for the tail of the market may be structurally unavailable; the CBCG-hosted filings become the only route.

negative_findings.description: WebFetch of https://www.ckb.me/... failed with 'unable to verify the first certificate'. This is a TLS chain/client issue, and the domain returns live content in search indexing.
negative_findings.result_summary: CKB pages recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive liveness pass could wrongly mark the market leader's disclosure hub as dead; the deterministic verifier should use a tolerant TLS chain or headless browser for ckb.me.

negative_findings.description: No bank published a machine-readable series of POS terminals installed or acquired volume; the only entity-level POS figure found was a marketing claim on CKB's corporate page (>4,000 terminals).
negative_findings.result_summary: POS estate data is narrative/marketing, not tabular.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bottom-up POS market sizing for Montenegro will need triangulation across marketing claims, tariff documents and locator scrapes rather than reported statistics.

brief: Bank-level card, ATM, POS and digital-channel numbers in Montenegro exist almost exclusively inside each bank's own Montenegrin-language annual report ('godišnji izvještaj o poslovanju'), audited statements, tariff schedules ('tarifnik'/'tarife i naknade') and securities prospectuses — no Montenegrin bank publishes an investor presentation. The strongest direct sources are CKB (OTP), NLB Banka, Hipotekarna banka, Erste Bank ME and Lovćen banka, each with a dedicated reports page; tail banks (Ziraat, Universal Capital, Zapad) appear to disclose only via the regulator. Three pointer layers make harvesting tractable: the CBCG registar banaka and its per-bank financial-statement and tariff comparators, the Montenegroberza/SCMN issuer filings (where bond prospectuses carry unusually rich network and card detail), and bankar.me's recurring bank-by-bank sector analyses. POS estate figures remain the weakest link — they surface as marketing claims and locator listings rather than reported series, so bottom-up POS sizing will require triangulation.
